nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a period pair and let $f$ be an elliptic function for $L$. Then the elliptic order of $f$ equals the elliptic order of $f$ in the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $0$. This holds by definition.
nodes.title: The elliptic order is the parallelogram order at vertex zero

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a period pair, let $f$ be an elliptic function for $L$ and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$. The elliptic order of $f$ in the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $\alpha$ is the natural number obtained by summing the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ over all points $z$ of the pole set of $f$ in that parallelogram, that is, over the points of the parallelogram where this multiplicity is nonzero.…
nodes.title: Elliptic order in a fundamental parallelogram

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a period pair and let $f$ be an elliptic function for $L$. The elliptic order of $f$ is its elliptic order in the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $0$: the sum of the pole multiplicities of $f$ over its poles in that parallelogram.
nodes.title: Elliptic order

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a period pair. For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$, the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $\alpha$ is a bounded subset of $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Fundamental parallelograms are bounded

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a period pair, let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be any function and let $\alpha, z \in \mathbb{C}$. Then $z$ lies in the pole set of $f$ in the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $\alpha$ if and only if $z$ lies in that parallelogram and the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is nonzero.
nodes.title: Membership in the pole set of a fundamental parallelogram

nodes.summary: For all $c, z \in \mathbb{C}$, the pole multiplicity at $z$ of the constant function with value $c$ is $0$. This includes the zero constant, whose meromorphic order at every point is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Pole multiplicity of a constant function

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be meromorphic on $U$ and let $z \in U$. Let $D(z)$ be the value at $z$ of the divisor of $f$ on $U$, that is, the order of $f$ at $z$, taken to be $0$ when that order is infinite. Then the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ equals $\max(0, -D(z))$.
nodes.title: Pole multiplicity via the divisor

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let the order of $f$ at $z$ be its meromorphic order, an element of $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ that is $0$ by convention when $f$ is not meromorphic at $z$. If this order is nonnegative (possibly $\infty$), then the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Pole multiplicity vanishes at points of nonnegative order

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. If $f$ is not meromorphic at $z$, then the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Pole multiplicity vanishes where the function is not meromorphic

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let the order of $f$ at $z$ be its meromorphic order, an element of $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ that is $0$ by convention when $f$ is not meromorphic at $z$. The pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is nonzero if and only if this order is negative, that is, if and only if $f$ has a pole at $z$.
nodes.title: Pole multiplicity is nonzero exactly at negative order

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a point $z \in \mathbb{C}$, let $\operatorname{ord}_z f \in \mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ be the meromorphic order of $f$ at $z$, which by convention is $0$ when $f$ is not meromorphic at $z$. The pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is the natural number $\max(0, -\operatorname{ord}_z f)$ when $\operatorname{ord}_z f$ is finite, and $0$ when…
nodes.title: Pole multiplicity

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a period pair, let $f$ be an elliptic function for $L$, and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$. Then the set of poles of $f$ in the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $\alpha$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finitely many poles in a fundamental parallelogram

nodes.summary: For a period pair $L$, a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a point $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$, the set of poles of $f$ in the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $\alpha$ is the set of points $z$ of that parallelogram at which the pole multiplicity of $f$ is nonzero.
nodes.title: Poles in a fundamental parallelogram

can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
